findings.description: The literal review-instruction command uses `printf %s '...\n'`, and bash printf does not expand backslash escapes in %s arguments, so the hook receives a trailing literal backslash-n and correctly fails closed with 'invalid pre-push object identity' (exit 1). Re-running the identical contract with a real newline (printf '%s\n', matching the handback's recorded command form) passes with exit 0. The fail-closed rejection of the malformed input is correct behavior per AC-4, not a defect.
findings.evidence: Observed directly: literal-\n invocation exited 1 with 'git-travel: cannot scan what is leaving the machine: invalid pre-push object identity'; real-newline invocation exited 0 with '1 unpublished commit(s)'.

findings.description: Live upstream origin/main (NousResearch/hermes-agent) advanced between implementation (b51c055a per the receipt) and this review (5ac75e91). This is external remote drift, not an implementation or review side effect: my before/after ls-remote values are identical, and the candidate's second parent b0ab2e1 remains reachable and remote-known. The hook's live-advertisement design (advertised_refs) is precisely what tolerates this.
